h1: Commercial vs Residential Playground Equipment: What's the Difference?

props.title: Commercial vs Residential Playground Equipment: What's the Difference?
props.summaryText: Why the swing set sold for a home garden is not the same as equipment for a school, society or park, and how to tell the two apart in a quote.
props.author: rohan-mehta
props.imageAlt: Commercial play structure with rope nets and a tepee climber at a residential township

takeaways.text: Commercial equipment is built for many children a day, every day, outdoors and with only occasional supervision.
Differences show in steel thickness, plastic quality, fixings, foundations, testing and warranty.
Housing societies, schools, parks and resorts all need commercial-grade equipment, even when the area is small.
Home play sets are fine for a private garden, but not for shared or public use.

faq.a: Commercial playground equipment is designed for public and shared spaces such as schools, housing societies, parks, resorts and malls. It is built to a recognised safety standard, uses heavier materials and fixings, is installed on proper foundations, and is meant to be used by many children every day for many years.

faq.q: Can a housing society use home play equipment?
faq.a: It is not advisable. A society play area is shared by many children, often without close supervision, and is used daily in all weather. Home play sets are not designed or tested for that load and usually lack the fixings, foundations and warranty needed for shared use.

faq.q: Why is commercial playground equipment more expensive?
faq.a: It uses thicker steel, better coatings, UV-stabilised plastic, vandal-resistant fixings and concrete foundations, and is designed and tested to safety standards. The extra cost is spread over a much longer life and many more users.

faq.q: How long does commercial playground equipment last?
faq.a: With proper installation and maintenance, well-made commercial equipment typically lasts many years outdoors. Moving parts such as swing hangers and bearings wear sooner and are replaced as part of normal maintenance.
